text:
matt: Heads up — Rivernode reporting increased 5xx rate on dedicated pools for the last 20m. Customer-impacting, SLA risk if this keeps up.
priya: saw the alert. Can someone from eng-platform own triage? Need a quick jaw check on rollback vs routing fallback.
kai: I can take initial triage for the next hour. Quick ask: is this a model-serving regression or infra (GPU OOM / queue saturation)?
matt: ops-bot logs show a spike in request latency and worker restarts around 16:12 UTC. No OOMs in kernel logs. Looks like KV cache pressure + long-tail batching.
simone: If it's KV cache pressure we can flip the fallback to smaller cache size for Rivernode routes and route heavy customers to burst tier. That is a config-only change — low risk.
jordan: what is the customer ask? They want an ETA for a mitigation and whether we can avoid a full rollback.
sarah-cs: Rivernode is seeing timeouts for checkout flows. They expect a mitigation within 2 hours or they'll enable their own fallback which will degrade UX. They asked for a written commitment.
priya: proposed plan — (1) kai triages and confirms cache pressure root cause (30m), (2) simone prepares a config patch to reduce per-worker kv retention and enable burst routing for Rivernode (45m), (3) jordan prepares customer-facing note and escalation timeline (30m). Can owners ack?
kai: ack. I have logs pulled and will validate root cause. If confirmed, I'll open a PR with `--hotfix` tag to the routing config repo.
simone: ack. I'll stage the config change in canary in us-west-2 and monitor p99. If stable for 10m we'll promote. I'll include a rollback flag.
jordan: ack. I'll draft the note and ping legal for SLA language. ETA 25m for first customer message.
priya: Thanks. Also reminder to include the fallback policy: automatic route to dedicated-burst, throttling at 120tps per tenant, and disable prefix caching for this customer for 1h. Simone/kai — add the exact commands in thread when you apply.
kai: copying commands here for ops runbook:
```
# reduce kv retention
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/serving-worker KV_CACHE_RETENTION=90
# enable burst routing for rivernode
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/routes/override -d '{"tenant":"rivernode","policy":"burst-tier"}'
```
simone: will run the canary at 17:05 UTC. If p99 drops below 800ms and 5xxs stop, we'll promote. If anything spikes, I revert using `kubectl rollout undo` and re-enable original cache.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4897 | Severity: P1 | Owner: kai | Pager: eng-oncall
matt: solid. Once we have canary green, please update this thread and customer note. Priya — can you commit to an internal SLO note so CS has the text for Rivernode's execs?
priya: will do. I'll post the first customer update in 30m and include next steps and owner contacts. :thumbsup:
simone: canary running now, will update within 12m.
kai: triage shows unusual caching churn tied to large multi-request batches from Rivernode. Confirming request signatures now.
jordan: thanks all. I'll stay on this thread until we have a stable mitigation or rollback. If anyone needs extra hands ping me directly.
simone: canary looks healthy at +7m — p99 down 45%, 5xxs gone. Promoting to prod with careful rollout.
kai: monitoring shows no worker restarts after canary promote. Marking triage as done.
priya: Customer update sent at 17:43 UTC: "we have deployed a targeted mitigation to reduce cache pressure; monitoring continues. Next update in 1h or sooner." Asked them to avoid traffic bursts in the meantime.
matt: closing loop — owners: kai (postmortem + triage doc), simone (config change + rollback), jordan (customer comms). Action items logged in Miro and will sync in standup tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :pray:
